description: A hunter left over from an age this country stopped telling, black-furred, amber-eyed, built for one rush.
lore: The fangs are longer than the jaw can shut over, so the mouth has to open the whole way before they are any use at all, and when it does you can see how little of the rest of the animal was built for anything else. Coat like wet coal. Eyes the colour of a lamp turned low. It came down out of a country far enough back that nothing walking around today has seen one of these standing up in life, and it has been out in the grass, more or less unmentioned, ever since.

Unmentioned is most of what is wrong with it. Other things get talked about badly — at the wrong fire, by somebody who only half saw them — and badly is still being held. This one does not come up. So it has gone the way untold things go, and the order is the sad part: the plain went first, then the weather on the plain, then whatever it used to be afraid of, then the others of its kind strung out along the line of a hunt. What is still out in the grass is the last hundred yards of one. It will lie in the open for hours doing nothing whatever, calm the way a cat is calm, which is not calm at all but a decision that has not been taken yet.

The leavings are honest about it. Coarse black mats of coat with other things' quills caught in them, off an animal that tried its luck on something quilled and ought to have walked past. A matched pair of glossy hooks, as sharp as the day they grew. Now and then a tooth hollowed at the root and gilded bright by somebody who thought the occasion called for that, and whoever it was is not around to say what the occasion had been. And under all of it, the piece that will not go any further down: grey, plated, shut around a clot of red. Of everything the animal used to be, what lasted was the part that took something back out of whatever it opened. Held against a blade it goes on doing exactly that, and it does not know how to do it by halves.

None of that came out of a telling. It was got by walking out to where one lies up and watching for a long while. The tellers will point out that being looked at is not the same as being told about; whoever wrote this down did not argue the point, and wrote it down.
